patches.rationale: The current export_rows naively joins cells with commas, so cells containing commas, quotes, or newlines produce invalid CSV that cannot round-trip through csv.reader. The fix routes each row through csv.writer with lineterminator='\n' to produce valid comma-delimited CSV with LF endings, preserving empty output and simple output. Unicode is preserved since csv.writer writes str cells directly. A new regression test file exercises the stated contracts: empty output, simple output, comma/quote/newline cells, Unicode, and round-tripping via csv.reader with exact input expressions and result types.

edits.old:
def export_rows(rows):
    return "".join(",".join(str(cell) for cell in row) + "\n" for row in rows)

contract_tests: tests/test_export_rows_csv.py::test_cell_with_comma_is_quoted asserts export_rows([["a,b", "c"]]) == '"a,b",c\n' and round-trips via csv.reader to [["a,b", "c"]].
tests/test_export_rows_csv.py::test_cell_with_quote_is_escaped asserts export_rows([['he said "hi"']]) == '"he said ""hi"""\n' and round-trips via csv.reader to [['he said "hi"']].

tests/test_export_rows_csv.py::test_cell_with_newline_is_quoted asserts export_rows([["line1
line2", "x"]]) == '"line1
line2",x
' and round-trips via csv.reader to [["line1
line2", "x"]].

tests/test_export_rows_csv.py::test_unicode_preserved asserts export_rows([["caf\u00e9", "\u4f60\u597d"]]) == "caf\u00e9,\u4f60\u597d\n" and round-trips via csv.reader to [["caf\u00e9", "\u4f60\u597d"]].
tests/test_export_rows_csv.py::test_lf_line_endings asserts "\r" not in export_rows([["a"], ["b"]]) and export_rows([["a"], ["b"]]) == "a\nb\n".

tests/test_export_rows_csv.py::test_round_trip_mixed asserts csv.reader(io.StringIO(export_rows(rows))) yields the original stringified cells for a mixed dataset including commas, quotes, newlines, and Unicode.
